newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late with softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late with softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Friday in quieter trade, with reports of softer weekend physical prices pressuring the complex though values were still within recent ranges.
At 1330 EDT, August slipped two cents to $2.155 per million British thermal units, while September was 1.8 cents lower at $2.10. Most others were steady to down two cents.

"We've got cash five cents over the screen, so I expect to see some convergence (between cash and futures), but I don't think August will expire far from here," said one Midwest trader, adding milder weather next week could pressure bidweek prices.
NYMEX August natgas futures expire Tuesday, July 29.

Chart traders agreed August remained stuck in a range, with support still seen at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance was now in the $2.20-21 area, with further selling likely at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.

Opinions were still mixed about market direction and few had strong convictions. While the bulls expected steady injection demand and favorable summer-to-winter spreads to support the market, the bears pointed to comfortable inventories and little extreme weather on the horizon.

"There are no hurricanes out there and we're coming into bidweek with some cooler weather. At some point, you have to get down to fundamentals," said one bearish trader, adding he expected September futures to be heavily pressured next month.
Based on recent AGA storage data, weekly injections need to average 67 bcf to get stocks back to 2.8 tcf by end-October ahead of the peak demand winter season.

In the cash Friday, weekend Gulf Coast prices slipped a couple of cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down a penny or two to the low-to-mid teens. New York city gate gas was also slightly lower at about $2.40.
NYMEX said 20,675 contracts traded at 1255 EDT. Hub open interest on July 24 rose 53 contracts to 208,231.
On the KCBT, August fell one cent to $2.09, while deferreds were still steady to two cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 6.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT August natgas futures expire Wednesday, July 30.
